---
title: "Sources & method"
---

## Principle

Every factual statement on this site links to a source. Wherever possible, that is a **primary source** — the legal text itself or the official statistics. My own assessments are labelled as such.

## Source hierarchy

| Rank | Type | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Original legal texts | EUR-Lex, gesetze-im-internet.de, announcements of China's Ministry of Ecology and Environment (mee.gov.cn) |
| 2 | Official data | German Environment Agency (UBA), Federal Network Agency (SMARD), National Energy Administration of China (NEA), National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS) |
| 3 | Scientific data processing | Fraunhofer ISE (Energy-Charts) |
| 4 | Secondary sources | e.g. ICAP, Ember — labelled, and only when no primary source is accessible |

Press articles and consultancy blogs serve at most as pointers to where the primary source can be found — they are not cited as evidence.

## Timeliness

- Every page carries a **"last checked" date**. Legal changes after that date are not reflected.
- Data pages are regenerated automatically (GitHub Actions); the retrieval date is shown with each chart.

## Data licences

- UBA data: [Data licence Germany – attribution 2.0](https://www.govdata.de/dl-de/by-2-0)
- Energy-Charts (Fraunhofer ISE): [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), source: Energy-Charts.info
- Other licences are stated with the respective dataset.

Please let me know via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/jinggling09/jinggling09.github.io/issues).
